edges.effect_quant: The main randomized signal suggests cognitive benefit from iron-fortified formula is concentrated in infants with lower hemoglobin or higher iron deficiency risk, whereas well-nourished or higher-iron-status infants generally show no clear developmental advantage.
edges.population: formula-fed infants, especially those with low hemoglobin or higher iron deficiency risk
edges.mechanism: Iron supports myelination, neurotransmitter synthesis, and energy metabolism during rapid brain development, so adequate iron delivery from formula is most likely to help infants who are closer to deficiency.
edges.summary: Iron-fortified formula appears most likely to help cognitive development in infants who start out with lower hemoglobin or higher iron deficiency risk. Trials in healthier or already iron-sufficient infants are usually neutral, so the beneficial direction is plausible but clearly conditional rather than universal.
edges.caveats: Too much iron may be unhelpful or even adverse in infants with already high hemoglobin, and several formula trials show no average developmental improvement in low-risk populations. This edge should therefore be interpreted as targeted benefit, not blanket enhancement.

evidence.citation: LozoffB et al 2012 Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med
